title: Francisco Goya's birth chart
metaDescription: Francisco Goya's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 9.7° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Aries — the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Mars. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 9.7° Aries — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mars. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Aries and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Mercury holds 12.7° Aries, Venus holds 8.8° Aries, Mars holds 22.8° Aries — in the old shorthand, a mind that decides at speaking speed; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Venus and Uranus: 0.3° from an exact sextile. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, the Sun conjunction Venus at 0.9°, and the Sun sextile Uranus at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Saturn while both square Neptune. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. Mars stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Six planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aries at 9.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; the Moon in Cancer at 12.7° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Venus in Aries at 8.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Aries at 22.8° is in domicile; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 15.1° is in domicile; Saturn in Libra at 11.2° is in exaltation. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 5 in fire, 3 in water, 2 in air by element, 7 cardinal, 2 fixed, 1 mutable by modality. A fire-weighted chart runs hot at the start line — initiative is its native language. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.0° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 12.7°.
